To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effective non-relativistic Schrödigner equation is exactly solved for two-fermi bound states in the presence of a massless vector boson, and the complete low-lying spectrum of bound states for different fine-structure constants and mass ratios is obtained.

the bound state solutions of the effective Schrödingerequation for the Yukawa model are obtained by solving a transcendental equation that involves the fine structure constant and the ratio of the constituent masses, and that the solutions are consistent in the limit of vanishing boson mass, and in the limit of infinite fermion mass.

the effective potential for a two-fermions bound state in the presence of a massless scalar field has an attractive Coulomb-like behavior for short distances, while for large distances it has an attractive Yukawa-like behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the bound states in a relativistic field theory.
the bound states of the Yukawa theory in the nonrelativisitc and one-body limit.
the bound state spectrum in Yukawa theory and its dependence on the fine structure constant and the constituent mass ratio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given value of the coupling constant, the bound states in Yukawa theory can be described in terms of the corresponding bound states in a Coulomb problem.
the nonrelativisitic approximation to the bound state problem in Yukawa theory is valid for any ratio of the constituent masses and for fine structure constants less than one.
, in the case of a massless vector boson, the Gell-Mamm-Low theorem is not applicable to bound state problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a generalization of the effective Schrödingerequation is obtained which allows for a systematic calculation of two-body bound states in a relativistic field theory.
the bound states in Yukawa theory are stable and that they are described by a Schrödinder equation of the form of a non-relativistic hydrogen atom.
the bound states in Yukawa theory are stable and that the mass spectrum of two-fermions is bounded by the sum of the two constituent masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a nontrivial bound state exists in Yukawa theory for any value of the fine structure constant α below unity, provided that the ratio of the constituent masses satisfies m1 < 1.2 m2.
the bound state masses are bounded from below by the constituent masses and that the binding energy is bounded from above by the sum of the constituent masses.
